shortDescription: A magical obsidian mirror used by Tezcatlipoca for divination and observing the world. It reflects all events, past, present, and future.

extendedContent.title: Origins & Mythology
extendedContent.content: The mirror's origins are inseparable from Tezcatlipoca's own. As one of the four primary gods who created the world, Tezcatlipoca's power and influence are immense. The mirror symbolizes his ability to see everything and his role as a judge of humanity. A prominent myth involves Tezcatlipoca using his own foot as bait, coated with the obsidian of his mirror, to lure the monstrous Cipactli, a primordial earth monster, during the creation of the Fifth Sun. In some versions of the myth, he loses his foot in the process, which is why he is sometimes depicted with a prosthetic leg made of obsidian or bone. This sacrifice highlights Tezcatlipoca's active role in shaping the cosmos and his willingness to endure hardship for the sake of creation.

extendedContent.title: Role & Significance
extendedContent.content: Tezcatlipoca's Mirror played a crucial role in Aztec cosmology and religious practice. It represented the god's all-seeing nature and his ability to intervene in human affairs. The mirror served as a constant reminder of the divine presence and the importance of moral conduct. It was believed that Tezcatlipoca could see into the hearts of people, discerning their true intentions and judging their actions accordingly. This belief instilled a sense of accountability and encouraged adherence to social norms and religious precepts. The mirror also functioned as a tool for divination, allowing priests and rulers to gain insight into the future and make informed decisions.

extendedContent.title: Symbolism & Interpretation
extendedContent.content: The mirror symbolizes several key concepts within Aztec thought. Firstly, it represents omniscience and the ability to perceive reality in its entirety. Secondly, it embodies the idea of reflection, both in the literal sense of reflecting images and in the metaphorical sense of reflecting upon one's own actions and motivations. The dark, polished surface of the obsidian mirror also evokes the idea of the unknown and the hidden aspects of reality. It suggests that there are always deeper layers of meaning and understanding to be uncovered. The 'smoking' aspect of the mirror, alluded to in Tezcatlipoca's name, can be interpreted as a symbol of transformation and the impermanence of all things.

extendedContent.title: Legacy & Influence
extendedContent.content: Tezcatlipoca's Mirror continues to fascinate scholars and artists interested in Aztec culture. The image of the smoking mirror has been used in various forms of art and literature to represent themes of power, knowledge, and the duality of human nature. The concept of a divine being who can see everything has resonated with audiences across cultures and continues to be explored in contemporary works of fiction and fantasy. The mirror serves as a potent symbol of the Aztec worldview, reminding us of the importance of self-reflection, moral responsibility, and the enduring power of the unseen world.

subtitle: A Window into the Soul of the World
name: Tezcatlipoca's Mirror
origin: The origin is tied to Tezcatlipoca himself; the mirror is often depicted as an integral part of his being, a tool he always possessed or crafted himself.
description: Tezcatlipoca's Mirror is a central artifact associated with the Aztec god Tezcatlipoca, whose name translates to 'Smoking Mirror.' This mirror, typically crafted from polished obsidian, served as a tool for divination, prophecy, and observing the actions of mortals and gods alike. It granted Tezcatlipoca omniscience, allowing him to perceive events across time and space. The mirror wasn't merely reflective; it was a portal, a window into the unseen realms and the hidden intentions of all beings. Tezcatlipoca was said to use the mirror to test humanity, rewarding the virtuous and punishing the wicked. The loss of a foot during the creation of the Fifth Sun is sometimes attributed to him using the mirror as bait to lure the earth monster Cipactli.
